passage:
Workers cleaning a storage room found old election posters from many years ago. The faces, slogans, and colors looked outdated.
Civics students studied them. They compared the issues on the posters with current political topics. Some concerns had changed. Others, like jobs, safety, and education, remained familiar.
The teacher reminded students that posters are designed to persuade, not simply inform. Students looked again and noticed large smiles, strong words, and promises without details.
The old posters became useful classroom tools.
Democracy requires more than voting. It requires reading carefully when people are trying to win your trust.

glossary.translation: 目前的；現行的；水流；電流
